chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people and said: 'Shall I inform you of the most evil of you?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The one who withholds his gifts, strikes his slave, and provisions himself alone.' So they thought that Allah had not created a creature more evil than this.

Then he said: 'Shall I inform you of the one who is more evil than that?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The one whose goodness is not hoped for, nor is there safety from his evil.' So they thought that Allah had not created a creature more evil than this.

Then he said: 'Shall I inform you of the one who is more evil than that?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'The foul-mouthed, cursing one, who when the believers are mentioned in his presence, he curses them, and when they mention him, they curse him.'

key_terms.لَا يُؤْمَنُ شَرُّهُ: nor is there safety from his evil
key_terms.لَا يُرْجَى خَيْرُهُ: whose goodness is not hoped for

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics of the most evil people according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a hierarchy of moral decay, culminating in the 'mutafahhish' (the excessively foul-mouthed), whose defining trait is the mutual cursing with the faithful, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social cohesion and the sanctity of the believers' community. The progression from material stinginess to spiritual unpredictability, and finally to vocal hostility, illustrates how internal character flaws manifest as external disruptions to the communal bond. This specific description of the 'mutafahhish' is often cited by scholars to define the characteristics of those who alienate themselves from the divine community through persistent verbal abuse.
